questions.q: What is the number of states in the minimal complete DFA over {0,1} that accepts strings containing 101 as a substring?
questions.exp: States track the matched prefix of 101 (ε, 1, 10) and a final trap state after 101: 4 states.

questions.q: Context-free languages are NOT closed under which operation?
questions.exp: CFLs are closed under union, concatenation and star, but intersection of {a^n b^n c^m} and {a^m b^n c^n} gives {a^n b^n c^n}, which is not CFL.

questions.q: In the triples representation of intermediate code, a result of an operation is referred to by
options: the position (index) of the triple that computes it
the name of a temporary variable
questions.exp: Triples have no explicit result field; later triples refer to earlier ones by their index.

questions.q: Which of the following context-free languages cannot be accepted by any deterministic PDA?
questions.exp: For w w^R the machine must guess the middle of the string, which needs nondeterminism; the others have a marker or fixed structure.

questions.q: Which system program combines several object modules and resolves references between them to produce an executable?
questions.exp: The linker resolves external symbol references across object modules.

questions.q:
Match each language with the smallest class containing it.
P: (ab)*   Q: {a^n b^n | n ≥ 1}   R: {a^n b^n c^n | n ≥ 1}   S: set of pairs (M,w) where TM M halts on w
1 Regular  2 CFL but not regular  3 CSL but not CFL  4 RE but not recursive
questions.exp: (ab)* is regular; a^n b^n is CFL; a^n b^n c^n is context-sensitive; the halting language is RE but not recursive.

questions.q: Compared with a subroutine call, the use of a macro generally results in
options: smaller object code and slower execution
smaller object code and faster execution
the same code size but extra stack usage
larger object code but no call/return overhead at run time
questions.exp: A macro body is copied inline at each call, increasing size but avoiding call and return overhead.

questions.q: A cross compiler is a compiler that
options: translates assembly code into machine code
executes the program statement by statement
runs on one machine but generates code for a different machine
questions.exp: The host and target architectures differ in a cross compiler.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Every regular language is context-free.
Reason (R): A PDA that ignores its stack can simulate any DFA.
Which is correct?
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Regular languages form a subset of CFLs because a PDA with unused stack behaves like a DFA.

questions.q: Dynamic linking resolves references to library routines
options: at load time or run time
questions.exp: Dynamic linking postpones resolution until the program is loaded or executed.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The language {a^n b^n | n ≥ 0} is not regular.
Reason (R): A DFA has only finite memory and cannot count an unbounded number of a's.
Which is correct?
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Matching the number of b's to a's needs unbounded counting, which a finite-state machine cannot provide.

questions.q:
Statement I: Every DFA is also an NFA.
Statement II: Every NFA can be converted into an equivalent DFA.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: A DFA is a special NFA, and subset construction converts any NFA to a DFA.

questions.q: Which of the following problems is decidable?
options: Whether a given Turing machine halts on a given input
Whether a given CFG is ambiguous
Whether two given CFGs generate the same language
Whether the language of a given DFA is empty
questions.exp: DFA emptiness is a reachability check on the state graph; the other problems are undecidable.

questions.q: Which of the following equals ∅* (the Kleene star of the empty set)?
questions.exp: By definition the star of any language includes the empty string, and ∅* = {ε}.

questions.q: In an assembler with 3-byte words, the program is: START 2000; LDA ALPHA; ADD BETA; STA GAMMA; ALPHA WORD 7; BETA RESW 2; GAMMA RESB 1. Each instruction occupies 3 bytes. What is the address assigned to GAMMA?
questions.exp: Three instructions occupy 2000-2008, ALPHA is at 2009, BETA at 2012 occupying 2 words = 6 bytes, so GAMMA is at 2018.

questions.q: Which property makes a grammar unsuitable for LL(1) predictive parsing?
options: Presence of terminals on right-hand sides
questions.exp: A left-recursive grammar makes a top-down parser loop forever and is never LL(1).

questions.q: In static single assignment (SSA) form of intermediate code,
options: every variable is assigned exactly once in the program text
every variable is used exactly once
questions.exp: SSA renames variables so each has a single definition, using phi functions at merge points.

questions.q: Eliminating left recursion from A → Aa | b gives
questions.exp: Standard transformation A → βA', A' → αA' | ε with α = a and β = b; it still generates b a*.

questions.q: What is the postfix form of the infix expression a*(b+c)-d?
questions.exp: b+c becomes bc+; a*(b+c) becomes abc+*; subtracting d gives abc+*d-.

questions.q: An NFA has 5 states. In the worst case, how many states can the equivalent DFA obtained by subset construction have?
questions.exp: Subset construction can produce up to 2^n states; 2^5 = 32.

questions.q: Which statement about pushdown automata is TRUE?
options: Deterministic and nondeterministic PDAs accept the same languages
A PDA with two stacks is equivalent to a PDA with one stack
Acceptance by final state and acceptance by empty stack define the same class of languages
PDAs accept exactly the regular languages
questions.exp: The two acceptance modes can be converted into each other; the other statements are false.

questions.q: How many distinct strings of length 4 are generated by the grammar S → aSb | SS | ε?
questions.exp: The grammar generates balanced a/b sequences; of length 4 they are aabb and abab.

questions.q: The Macro Name Table and Macro Definition Table of a two-pass macro processor are built during
options: Pass 1, while recognizing and saving macro definitions
questions.exp: Pass 1 stores definitions; Pass 2 uses them to expand calls.

questions.q: Which of the following problems is undecidable?
options: Whether a given DFA accepts a given string
Whether a given CFG generates a given string
Whether a given regular expression matches the empty string
Whether a given Turing machine halts on a given input
questions.exp: The halting problem is the classic undecidable problem; the others are decidable.

questions.q: In x = (a+b)*c; y = (a+b)*d; with a and b unchanged between the statements, how many addition operations remain after common subexpression elimination?
questions.exp: a+b is computed once and reused, so one addition remains.

questions.q: Which option correctly shows the proper containment of language classes?
questions.exp: The Chomsky hierarchy is Type 3 ⊂ Type 2 ⊂ Type 1 ⊂ Type 0.

questions.q: What is the number of states in the minimal DFA for the language of (a+b)*abb?
questions.exp: The DFA tracks the longest suffix matching a prefix of abb: states for ε, a, ab, abb, so 4 states.

questions.q: Which of the following languages is NOT regular?
options: strings over {a,b} with an even number of a's
questions.exp: a^n b^n requires unbounded counting, which a finite automaton cannot do; the pumping lemma shows it is not regular.

questions.q: A DFA has two states q0 (start and accepting) and q1. Input 0 toggles between q0 and q1, and input 1 keeps the state unchanged. Which string is accepted?
questions.exp: The DFA accepts iff the number of 0s is even. 10110 has two 0s; 0001 has three, 1011 has one, 111000 has three.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of strength reduction?
options: Merging two identical expressions into one
questions.exp: Strength reduction replaces an expensive operation (multiplication) by a cheaper one (shift).

questions.q: Which of the following grammars is ambiguous?
options: E → E+T | T ; T → T*F | F ; F → id
questions.exp: The string id+id*id has two distinct parse trees under E → E+E | E*E | id.

questions.q: The halting problem for Turing machines is
questions.exp: A universal TM can simulate M on w and accept if it halts, so the language is RE, but no TM decides it for all inputs.

questions.q: How many strings of length 3 over {0,1} belong to the language of the regular expression 0*1*?
questions.exp: Strings are 0^i 1^(3-i) for i = 0..3: 111, 011, 001, 000, which are 4 strings.

questions.q: For the grammar S → aAb, A → cA | ε, what is FOLLOW(A)?
questions.exp: A appears only just before b in S → aAb, and A → cA places A at the end of a right-hand side, adding FOLLOW(A) to itself; so FOLLOW(A) = {b}.

questions.q: In panic-mode error recovery, the parser
options: discards input symbols until it finds a synchronizing token
replaces the erroneous symbol by a default value
questions.exp: Panic mode skips input until a delimiter such as a semicolon allows parsing to resume.

questions.q:
Match the compiler phase with its output.
1 Lexical analysis  2 Syntax analysis  3 Semantic analysis  4 Code optimization
P: Parse tree  Q: Stream of tokens  R: Type-checked annotated tree  S: Improved intermediate code
questions.exp: Lexical analysis yields tokens, parsing yields a parse tree, semantic analysis yields an annotated tree, and optimization yields improved code.

questions.q: Relocation information in an object module is used by the loader to
options: check the syntax of the program
find which words must be adjusted when the program is loaded at a different base address
questions.exp: Words holding addresses are flagged so the loader can add the load-address offset to them.

questions.q: Which of the following phases of a compiler is machine dependent?
questions.exp: Code generation produces target machine code and depends on the target architecture.

questions.q: What is the main task of Pass 1 of a two-pass assembler?
options: Generate final object code with all operands resolved
Assign addresses to labels and build the symbol table
Resolve references to symbols in other modules
Relocate the program at load time
questions.exp: Pass 1 scans the source, maintains the location counter and records label addresses in the symbol table; code is generated in Pass 2.

questions.q: The regular expression (a+b)*a(a+b) describes strings over {a,b} in which
options: the second symbol from the right end is a
the second symbol from the left is a
questions.exp: a(a+b) at the end means an a followed by exactly one more symbol, so a is second from the end.

questions.q: The forward reference problem in assembly language is usually solved by
questions.exp: The first pass collects all label addresses so the second pass can resolve forward references.

questions.q: A universal Turing machine is one that
options: simulates any Turing machine given its description and input
questions.exp: A UTM takes an encoding of a machine M and input w and simulates M on w.

questions.q: To obtain a DFA for the complement of a regular language from a complete DFA, we
questions.exp: In a complete DFA a string is rejected exactly when it ends in a non-final state, so swapping accepting status complements the language.
a becomes 2+3 = 5 (x = 5); then b = 5 - 3 = 2 (y = 2).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a task of the lexical analyzer?
options: Keeping track of line numbers for error messages
questions.exp: Checking balanced parentheses requires a stack and belongs to the parser.

questions.q:
Consider the code:
1 a = 1
2 if a > 5 goto 6
3 b = 2
4 c = 3
5 goto 7
6 b = 4
7 print b
How many basic blocks does it contain?
questions.exp: Leaders are statements 1, 3 (after a conditional jump), 6 (jump target and after a goto) and 7 (jump target). Blocks: 1-2, 3-5, 6, 7.

questions.q: How many three-address instructions are generated for a = b + c*d - e, using temporaries for each intermediate result and a final assignment?
questions.exp: t1 = c*d; t2 = b + t1; t3 = t2 - e; a = t3 gives 4 instructions.

questions.q: A PDA for {a^n b^n | n ≥ 1} pushes one symbol A on the stack for each a and pops one A for each b. After reading aaabb, how many A symbols are on the stack?
questions.exp: Three pushes and two pops leave 3 - 2 = 1 symbol A.

questions.q: If both a language L and its complement are recursively enumerable, then L is
questions.exp: Run the two recognizers in parallel; exactly one halts and accepts, giving a decider.

questions.q: In a language where else is a keyword, the lexical analyzer reads the input elsewhere using the longest-match (maximal munch) rule. What does it return?
options: the keyword else followed by an identifier where
questions.exp: Maximal munch picks the longest lexeme that matches a token pattern, which is the identifier elsewhere.

questions.q: For the grammar S → AB, A → a | ε, B → b, what is FIRST(S)?
questions.exp: FIRST(S) = FIRST(A) minus ε, plus FIRST(B) because A is nullable; B is not nullable so ε is excluded.

questions.q: Which regular expression is equivalent to (a+b)*?
questions.exp: (a*b*)* can generate any sequence of a's and b's by repeating blocks, so it equals (a+b)*.

questions.q: In graph-coloring register allocation, an edge between two nodes means
options: the two variables are live at the same time and cannot share a register
the two variables must be in the same register
one variable is a copy of the other
they appear in the same statement
questions.exp: Nodes are live ranges; an interference edge forces different colors (registers).

questions.q: Type-1 (context-sensitive) grammars are recognized by which machine?
options: Turing machine with unbounded extra tape only
questions.exp: Context-sensitive languages are exactly those accepted by nondeterministic linear bounded automata.

questions.q: A DFA with 7 states accepts at least one string of length 9. What must be true of its language?
questions.exp: A string of length at least the number of states forces a repeated state, so a loop can be pumped to give infinitely many accepted strings.

questions.q:
Statement I: Regular languages are closed under complement.
Statement II: Context-free languages are closed under complement.
Which is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.exp: Swapping final and non-final states of a complete DFA complements a regular language; CFLs are not closed under complement.

questions.q: Which function is NOT performed by an absolute loader?
options: Placing the object code into memory
Transferring control to the program's starting address
Relocation of the program to a different address
questions.exp: An absolute loader just loads code at the addresses specified in the object program; no relocation is done.

questions.q: Checking that the operands of an arithmetic operator have compatible types is the job of which compiler phase?
questions.exp: Type checking needs symbol-table information and is done in semantic analysis.

questions.q:
Consider the code:
1 a = 4
2 b = a + 1
3 a = 9
4 c = b * 2
5 print(c)
Which statement is dead code that can be removed without changing the output?
questions.exp: The value 9 assigned to a in statement 3 is never used afterwards; statement 1 is needed by statement 2.

questions.q: How many target instructions are needed for a = b + c on a simple load-store machine with registers, using LD, ADD and ST instructions?
questions.exp: LD R1,b; LD R2,c; ADD R1,R1,R2; ST a,R1 are 4 instructions.

questions.q: Which of the following languages is NOT context-free?
questions.exp: The copy language ww cannot be handled by a stack; the pumping lemma for CFLs rules it out.

questions.q: A Turing machine moves right, replacing every 0 by 1 and every 1 by 0, and halts at the first blank. If the tape initially holds 01101, what does it hold after halting?
questions.exp: Flipping each bit of 01101 gives 10010.

questions.q: A context-free language for which every grammar is ambiguous is called
questions.exp: This is the definition of an inherently ambiguous language, such as {a^i b^j c^k | i = j or j = k}.

questions.q: A macro ADDM &X,&Y is defined with body LDA &X and ADD &Y. After the calls ADDM P,Q and ADDM R,S, how many instruction lines appear in the expanded program?
questions.exp: Each call expands into two lines (LDA and ADD), so two calls give 4 lines.

questions.q: What is the number of states in the minimal DFA that accepts binary strings representing numbers divisible by 5?
questions.exp: The DFA tracks the remainder modulo 5, requiring 5 states.

questions.q: YACC is a tool that generates
questions.exp: YACC builds LALR(1) parsers from grammar specifications; Lex generates lexical analyzers.

questions.q: Languages that allow recursive procedures normally require
questions.exp: Each active call needs its own activation record, naturally managed on a stack.

questions.q: In a block-structured language, when a name is used, the compiler first searches the symbol table of
options: the innermost (current) scope, then enclosing scopes
the outermost scope first, then inner scopes
questions.exp: The most closely nested declaration hides outer ones, so lookup proceeds from inner to outer scopes.

questions.q: The Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) is
questions.exp: PCP is a classic undecidable problem proved by reduction from the halting problem.

questions.q: Given E → TE', E' → +TE' | ε, T → FT', T' → *FT' | ε, F → (E) | id, what is FOLLOW(F)?
questions.exp: FOLLOW(F) includes * from T', and since T' is nullable it includes FOLLOW(T) = {+, ), $}.

questions.q: Replacing the expression 3 * 4 + 2 with 14 at compile time is called
questions.exp: Evaluating constant expressions during compilation is constant folding.

questions.q: What is the number of states in the minimal DFA over {0,1} that accepts all strings in which the number of 0s is divisible by 3?
questions.exp: Only the count of 0s modulo 3 matters, giving three equivalence classes: 0, 1, 2.

questions.q: A complete DFA has states A (start), B, C, D with final states C and D. Transitions: A-0->B, A-1->C, B-0->A, B-1->D, C-0->C, C-1->C, D-0->D, D-1->D. How many states does the minimal equivalent DFA have?
questions.exp: C and D are equivalent (both always stay accepting); A and B are equivalent (both go to accepting states on 1 and swap on 0). So 2 classes.

questions.q: A Moore machine is given an input string of length n. The length of its output string is
questions.exp: A Moore machine outputs a symbol for the start state before reading any input, so it produces n + 1 symbols.

questions.q: The grammar S → aSb | ε generates which language?
options: {w ∈ {a,b}* | w has equal number of a's and b's}
questions.exp: Each application of S → aSb adds one a on the left and one b on the right, so strings are a^n b^n.

questions.q: What is the number of states in the minimal DFA for the language of strings over {a,b} whose third symbol from the right end is a?
questions.exp: The DFA must remember the last 3 symbols, requiring 2^3 = 8 states, and this is minimal.

questions.q: For a string derived from an unambiguous context-free grammar, how many leftmost derivations does it have?
options: n, where n is the string length
questions.exp: A grammar is unambiguous exactly when every string has a unique leftmost derivation.

questions.q: In Greibach normal form, every production has the form
options: A → aα, where a is a terminal and α is a string of variables (possibly empty)
A → αβ, where α and β are terminals
questions.exp: GNF requires each right-hand side to start with exactly one terminal followed by variables.

questions.q: For the augmented grammar S' → S, S → aS | b, how many states are in the canonical LR(0) collection of items?
questions.exp: States: I0 start, goto on S, goto on b, goto on a (I2 with self-loop on a), and goto from I2 on S: 5 states.

questions.q: An NFA over {a,b} has states p (start), q, r with r final. p-a->{p,q}, p-b->{p}, q-b->{r}, and there are no other transitions. How many states (excluding the empty set) does the subset construction produce?
questions.exp: Reachable subsets: {p}; on a {p,q}; from {p,q} on a {p,q}, on b {p,r}; from {p,r} on a {p,q}, on b {p}. Total 3.

questions.q: An NFA has states q0, q1, q2 over {a,b}. q0 loops on a and b, q0 --a--> q1, q1 --b--> q2, and q2 loops on a and b. q2 is the only final state. What does it accept?
options: strings containing ab as a substring
questions.exp: The machine guesses an ab, then accepts whatever follows, so any string containing ab is accepted.

questions.q: Which representation keeps only operators and operands and omits grammar non-terminals from the derivation?
questions.exp: An abstract syntax tree is a condensed form of the parse tree retaining the essential structure.

questions.q: The grammar S → AB, A → aA | a, B → bB | b generates
options: zero or more a's followed by zero or more b's
strings with equal numbers of a's and b's
strings of alternating a and b
one or more a's followed by one or more b's
questions.exp: A derives a+ and B derives b+, so S derives a+b+.

questions.q: When converting a context-free grammar into an equivalent PDA that accepts by empty stack, the minimum number of PDA states needed is
options: equal to the number of variables
questions.exp: The standard construction uses a single state, with the stack simulating leftmost derivations.

questions.q: Which data structure is most commonly used to implement a symbol table when fast insertion and lookup are needed?
questions.exp: A hash table gives average constant-time insertion and lookup of identifiers.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT stored in an activation record of a procedure?
questions.exp: Activation records hold run-time data such as return address, parameters and locals, not the source code.

questions.q: Three-address code is generated for a = b*c + d*e, with no temporary reused. How many temporaries are needed?
questions.exp: t1 = b*c; t2 = d*e; t3 = t1 + t2; a = t3 uses three temporaries.

questions.q: In the pumping lemma for regular languages with pumping length p, a long string w is split as xyz. Which conditions must hold?
questions.exp: The lemma requires y to be non-empty and the loop to occur within the first p symbols.

questions.q: Which statement about an interpreter is correct?
options: It always executes faster than compiled code
It first converts the entire program into machine code
It translates and executes the program statement by statement without producing a persistent object program
It always requires a separate linker
questions.exp: An interpreter processes source statements one at a time at run time.

questions.q: What is the number of states in the minimal complete DFA over {a,b} that accepts exactly the strings of length 3?
questions.exp: States count symbols read 0, 1, 2, 3 and one dead state for length > 3: total 5.

questions.q: Deterministic context-free languages are closed under
questions.exp: DCFLs are closed under complement but not under union, intersection or concatenation.

questions.q: Deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines are equivalent in
options: the class of languages they accept
the space used for every language
questions.exp: Any NTM can be simulated by a DTM, though possibly with exponential slowdown.

questions.q: Which of the following machines is strictly LESS powerful than a standard single-tape Turing machine?
options: Turing machine with a two-way infinite tape
questions.exp: Multi-tape, nondeterministic and two-way tape variants all accept the same languages as a standard TM; a PDA accepts only CFLs.

questions.q:
For the code:
1 a = b + c
2 d = a * 2
3 a = 5
4 e = d + a
and assuming e is used later, which variables are live immediately after statement 1?
questions.exp: After statement 1, only a is used (in statement 2) before being redefined; d is defined at statement 2, and b, c are not used later.

questions.q: Which of the following strings does NOT belong to the language of the regular expression (a+b)*abb?
questions.exp: Every string in the language must end with abb; abbb ends with bbb.

questions.q: The dangling-else problem leads to which kind of parsing conflict?
questions.exp: On seeing else, the parser can either shift it (attach to nearest if) or reduce the inner if statement.

questions.q: Moving a computation that gives the same result in every iteration out of a loop is called
questions.exp: Hoisting invariant expressions out of the loop body is code motion.

questions.q: How many strings of length 5 over {a,b} belong to the language of (a+b)*bb?
questions.exp: The last two symbols are fixed as bb; the first 3 symbols are free, giving 2^3 = 8 strings.

questions.q: In the grammar E → E+E | E*E | a, how many distinct parse trees does the string a+a*a have?
questions.exp: It can be parsed as (a+a)*a or as a+(a*a), giving 2 parse trees.

questions.q: Peephole optimization works by
options: analysing the whole program flow graph
optimizing only the source code before parsing
examining a small window of adjacent target instructions and replacing them with better ones
questions.exp: A peephole optimizer slides a small window over the generated code and applies local improvements.

questions.q: Which string is generated by the grammar S → aSa | bSb | c?
questions.exp: Each step wraps S with matching symbols, so the strings are w c w^R; abcba = ab c ba.

questions.q: An unresolved external reference arises when
options: a symbol is used in one module but defined in none of the modules being linked
two modules define the same symbol
a symbol is defined but never used
a label is defined twice in the same module
questions.exp: The linker cannot find a definition for the referenced symbol.

questions.q: Rice's theorem states that
options: every non-trivial semantic property of the language accepted by a Turing machine is undecidable
every property of Turing machines is decidable
the halting problem is decidable for deterministic machines
questions.exp: Any property of the accepted language that some, but not all, RE languages have cannot be decided.

questions.q: A Mealy machine differs from a Moore machine because its output depends on
options: both the current state and the current input
questions.exp: In a Mealy machine, outputs are attached to transitions, so they depend on state and input.

questions.q: A grammar in Chomsky normal form derives a string of length 5 (no ε). How many derivation steps are needed?
questions.exp: A string of length n needs n-1 binary productions and n terminal productions, so 2n - 1 = 9 steps.

questions.q: The intersection of a context-free language and a regular language is
questions.exp: Run the PDA and the DFA together using product construction; the result is a PDA.

questions.q: Among the following parsers, which is the most powerful (accepts the largest class of grammars)?
questions.exp: CLR(1) accepts every grammar accepted by SLR(1) and LALR(1), and LL(1) grammars are a subset of LR(1).

questions.q: Which of the following is an assembler directive (pseudo-operation) rather than a machine instruction?
questions.exp: EQU defines a symbol's value for the assembler and generates no machine code.

questions.q: A pushdown automaton is a finite automaton equipped with
questions.exp: The stack gives a PDA unbounded last-in-first-out memory.

questions.q: How many tokens does a lexical analyzer produce for the C statement: int x = a + b * 3;
questions.exp: Tokens: int, x, =, a, +, b, *, 3, ; which makes 9.

questions.q: The right-linear grammar S → aS | bA, A → aA | ε generates which language?
questions.exp: S generates any number of a's, then one b, then A generates any number of a's.

questions.q: Why is the grammar S → aS | a not LL(1)?
options: Both alternatives begin with a, so their FIRST sets overlap and left factoring is needed
questions.exp: With one lookahead symbol a the parser cannot choose between the two productions.

questions.q: In bottom-up parsing, a handle is
options: a substring used in a leftmost derivation step
the first terminal in the input
the top symbol of the parse stack always
a substring matching a production's right side whose reduction is a step of a reverse rightmost derivation
questions.exp: Reducing the handle at each step traces a rightmost derivation in reverse.

questions.q: Which statement about recursive languages is TRUE?
options: They are not closed under intersection
They are the same as recursively enumerable languages
They form a proper subset of the context-free languages
questions.exp: A decider can be modified to swap accept and reject, so recursive languages are closed under complement.

questions.q: Which error is detected by the lexical analyzer?
options: A missing semicolon at the end of a statement
A character that cannot begin any valid token, such as @ in a C program
Adding an integer to a string
questions.exp: Invalid characters fail to match any token pattern, which is a lexical error; the others are syntax or semantic errors.

questions.q: For the grammar E → TE', E' → +TE' | ε, T → id, what is FOLLOW(T)?
questions.exp: FOLLOW(T) contains FIRST(E') minus ε = {+}, and since E' is nullable also FOLLOW(E) = {$}.

questions.q: The regular expression (0+1)*01(0+1)* describes the set of binary strings that
questions.exp: Anything may precede and follow the 01, so the language is all strings containing the substring 01.

questions.q: How many tokens are there in: if (a >= 10) b = a;
questions.exp: Tokens: if, (, a, >=, 10, ), b, =, a, ; which makes 10.

questions.q: Consider the grammar S → AB | a, A → aA, B → b. After removing useless symbols, what remains?
options: S → AB | a and B → b
the grammar generates the empty language
questions.exp: A is non-generating, so S → AB is removed, making B unreachable; only S → a remains.

questions.q: An ε-NFA has transitions q0 --ε--> q1, q1 --ε--> q2 and q2 --a--> q3. How many states are in ε-closure(q0)?
questions.exp: From q0 we reach q1 and q2 by ε moves, so the closure is {q0, q1, q2}.
